title: Surface accordion workspace hopper and adaptive left-rail IA
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define an information architecture for a compact, progressive left rail that surfaces a workspace "hopper" using an accordion pattern. The goal is to reduce cognitive overhead for users with many workspaces while keeping quick access to rollouts, cost lenses, and per-route dashboards. This ticket captures the high-fidelity prototype, accessibility pass, and implementation constraints for the navigation component. The design explores three interaction modes: collapsed (micro-chips), grouped-accordion (workspace hubs with affinity buckets), and expanded (full workspace list). It also proposes a persistent cost bubble tied to the active route and a dedicated rollouts lane to surface canary/A-B traffic and rollout health at a glance.
acceptance_criteria: Left rail prototype in Figma with collapsed / grouped-accordion / expanded states
Accessible keyboard and screen-reader flows documented (ARIA patterns)
Hand-off spec for engineering including component states, animations, and telemetry hooks
Usability notes from at least 5 product/engineer stakeholder sessions incorporated
Performance constraints documented: initial render budget <120ms for 200 workspaces
notes: Trade-off: accordion grouping reduces surface area but adds one tap for deep workspace switching; chosen to prioritize speed-to-main-workspace for 80% of sessions.
Telemetry: we propose new event namespace nav.workplace.* to record expand/collapse and persistent-bubble interactions; ENG has flagged sampling to avoid event storming.
Cost bubble: shows 7d spend, 24h delta, and top contributor model; clicking opens route cost-view panel (single-panel overlay).
Rollouts lane: summary chips (green/yellow/red) for active rollouts; UX should support drill-to-rollout in console without leaving context.
Constraint: backend cannot return full workspace metadata on initial load; design uses lightweight index + lazy load for richer badges (billing, SSO status, rollout presence).
